topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture topic, outlines learning outcomes, and reviews the multi-step progression model and framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and oncogenic signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases confer growth signal independence and resistance to inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks to terminal differentiation maintain proliferative states in hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and dysregulation of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by reactivating telomerase, overcoming telomere shortening, and bypassing p53-mediated senescence checkpoints.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic rewiring, and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites that drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why expanding tumors require the angiogenic switch to recruit new blood vessels for oxygen and nutrient perfusion.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metastatic cascade, clinical monitoring via circulating tumor cells, metastatic inefficiency under the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the interconnected nature of cancer hallmarks, references advanced frameworks, and concludes the session.
